title: CXR, CAD, and triage
dek: Chest radiography is a sensitive triage tool, not a microbiologic proof. Computer-aided detection is a WHO-endorsed reader for screening adults — still a score, still a pretest-probability problem.
story: CXR is among the most sensitive simple screens for pulmonary TB, and among the least specific. Scars, bronchiectasis, silicosis, cancer, and old granulomas all light up. WHO uses CXR in screening and in ruling out disease before TPT; it never licensed CXR as culture.

Computer-aided detection (CAD) software reads digital CXRs and emits a score. WHO (2021 screening module, carried forward) conditionally recommends CAD for screening/triage in people ≥15 years, HIV-positive or not, as a replacement for human reader in those use cases. Thresholds are product- and prevalence-specific.

A high CAD score in a 1% prevalence community survey is mostly false positives. The same score in a symptomatic clinic is a different posterior. That sentence is the entire point of the predictive-values plate — radiology is not exempt.
deep: Pediatric chests and extrapulmonary disease are outside the adult CAD endorsement. Do not run a toddler through an adult CAD SOP and call it WHO.
CAD does not speciate, does not grade RIF, and does not distinguish old scar from new cavity without a human and a NAAT.
CRP ≥5 mg/L is a WHO screening tool for people with HIV, not a CAD equivalent, but it lives on the same triage shelf.
Programmes must pick a threshold calibrated to their prevalence and their WRD capacity. Copy-pasting a vendor’s European cut-point is how you drown the lab.

visual.caption: Schematic CAD-score distributions in people with and without TB. The dashed threshold is a policy choice: move it right to raise PPV and miss cases; move it left to catch cases and flood confirmatory testing.

example.title: Community screen, CAD ≥ 0.65, prevalence 0.8%
example.setup: Vendor claims Se 0.90, Sp 0.70 at threshold 0.65. 10,000 people screened.

steps.title: Expected true cases
steps.body: 80 people with TB if prevalence is 0.8%. Se 0.90 catches 72.

steps.title: PPV
steps.body: 72 / (72 + 2,976) ≈ 2.4%. Almost everyone you send for Xpert is negative. That is not CAD failing; that is Bayes.

example.takeaway: CAD thresholds are prevalence-dependent policy, not microbiology.

check.prompt: WHO’s CAD recommendation is best summarised as:
choices: CAD replaces culture in children under 5
CAD may replace human CXR readers for screening/triage in people ≥15 years, with thresholds set to context
CAD is required before every 3HP dose
check.answer: CAD may replace human CXR readers for screening/triage in people ≥15 years, with thresholds set to context
check.why: Adult screening tool, not a DST.

whyWrong.CAD is required before every 3HP dose: CXR helps rule out disease; CAD is not a pill-gate.
